question.text: A short straddle has maximum profit of:

answer.text: Total premium received (call premium + put premium)
The difference between the call and put premiums

explanation.text: The Logic: Short straddle = sell call + sell put at the same strike. Max profit = total premium received. In the workbook table, at the 83 strike this is Rs. 0.35 (0.20 call premium + 0.15 put premium), realised when USDINR closes exactly at the strike. The Trap: Short straddle has limited profit but unlimited loss; max profit for SHORT straddle = max LOSS for long straddle. Note: Short straddle sellers bet on stability — they profit if USDINR stays between the two BEPs. Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, pp.109-111 (short-straddle table on p.110).
